description: WifiHaven Plain support integration (#2199 + #2200, epic #2197): server-signed widget-identity outcomes, household→Plain customer-upsert outcomes, the #2200 Claude responder's webhook outcomes (support_ai_draft_total{outcome,reason} from SupportResponder — dispatched / skipped_unauthenticated / rate_limited / invalid_signature / malformed / disabled / error), and the cloud agent's callback actions (support_agent_action_total{op,outcome} — reply / issue / household_read). All labels are bounded enums (never per-email / per-household / per-thread). The responder runs iff the explicit support.responderEnabled flag is set (#2265 — no dark-by-default; a true flag with missing config refuses to boot); disabled installs count outcomes as disabled and dispatch nothing. See issues #2206, #2200, #2241, #2265. #2419 adds the data-access consent lifecycle (support_consent_total{outcome} — the agent's REQUEST vs the customer's grant/revoke, plus the household-mismatch guard): consent is recorded server-side from the customer's own authenticated action, so the agent can ask but can never self-grant. #2438 adds support_dispatch_total{outcome,transport} — the dispatcher-level cloud-trigger outcome (dispatched / error / disabled) at the transport boundary, isolating a silent non-2xx trigger failure the conflated draft metric can't surface.

panels.title: Widget identity requests (cumulative, issued)
panels.description: sum(support_widget_identity_total{outcome="issued"}) — total server-signed identities issued to authenticated admins. Zero while the widget is dark (no Plain app id / identity secret).

panels.title: Widget identity rate by outcome
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_widget_identity_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — issued / no_email (caller has no email to identify — username-only admin) / disabled (Plain widget unconfigured, feature dark). A rising no_email share means admins without an email are opening the app; disabled dominates until the operator provisions the Plain widget keys.

panels.title: Household → Plain customer upsert outcomes
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_customer_upsert_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — ok (mapping written to Plain) / disabled (Plain write API unconfigured — no API key, dark) / error (Plain returned non-2xx or a GraphQL error; fail-open, the identity response is unaffected). A persistent 'error' share means the household→customer mapping isn't reaching Plain — check the API key / GraphQL endpoint.

panels.title: Responder webhook outcomes (#2200)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — dispatched (a cloud-agent session was created for a UI-originated thread) / email_registered_dispatched (#2307: a NEW inbound email whose From matched a registered household admin, admitted to the AI bound to that household) / email_unregistered_rejected (#2307: a NEW inbound email from an unregistered address got the FIXED static reject — NO Claude call, NO tokens burned) / skipped_unauthenticated (a continuation with no resolvable tenant) / skipped_not_inbound (#2403 loop guard: our own outbound thread.chat_sent reply, a non-customer actor, or a bodyless metadata event — never dispatched) / rate_limited (the per-thread + global dispatch, or the global reject, cost caps fired) / invalid_signature (unsigned or forged webhook — security-relevant, investigate a sustained rate) / malformed / disabled (responder dark) / error (Managed Agents dispatch failed). Emitted by SupportResponder.handleWebhook.

panels.title: Agent callback actions (#2200/#2241)
panels.description: sum by (op, outcome) (rate(support_agent_action_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the dispatched cloud agent's token-authenticated callbacks: reply (post the AI-attributed reply into the token-bound Plain thread — sent to the customer, autonomous send), issue (file a PII-scrubbed, support-agent-labeled GitHub issue), household_read (the consented single-household summary). outcome=denied covers bad/expired tokens AND consent-less household reads; rate_limited is the per-thread/global issue caps. Emitted by SupportResponder.

panels.title: Agent-filed issues (24h) — volume alert feed
panels.description: sum(increase(support_agent_action_total{env="$env",op="issue",outcome="ok"}[24h])) — GitHub issues the support agent filed in the last 24h (the #2241 volume-alert feed). The per-thread (3/h) + global (10/h) rate limits cap the ceiling; a value near the cap means the agent is filing aggressively — review the support-agent label on GitHub.

panels.title: Agent sessions dispatched (24h) — cost watch
panels.description: sum(increase(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="dispatched"}[24h])) — cloud-agent sessions started in the last 24h. Each session bills API tokens (rough order: $0.10–$0.50/draft on Sonnet 5); the global dispatch cap (50/day) bounds the ceiling. Red at the cap = sustained widget spam or a webhook retry loop — check the rate_limited outcome on the webhook panel.

panels.title: Household → Plain tenant entitlement upsert outcomes (#2240)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_tenant_upsert_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the household→Plain TENANT write (household name + plan/founding tenant fields), separate from the customer upsert. ok (name + all fields written) / error (tenant upsert failed, or a field write failed). Fail-open, the identity response is unaffected. This panel is the aggregate; the '#2410' panel next to it slices error by reason so a PROVISIONING GAP (permission / schema — needs a fix) is distinguishable from a transient tenant/field hiccup.

panels.title: Entitlement write failures by reason — provisioning-gap watch (#2410)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(support_tenant_upsert_total{env="$env",outcome="error"}[5m])) — WHY the household→Plain entitlement write failed. permission (the machine-user API key lacks the tenantField:* permission — grant it, docs/ops/plain-setup.md §5.1) and schema (the plan/founding tenant-field schemas are not registered in the Plain workspace — register them, docs/ops/plain-setup.md §7.3) are PROVISIONING GAPS: they will NEVER self-heal until fixed, and the API also logs each at ERROR with the fix inline. tenant / field_write are the transient/other bucket (a Plain hiccup — usually self-heals). ALERT on any sustained permission or schema rate; a transient tenant/field_write blip is expected noise.

panels.title: Data-access consent lifecycle (#2419)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_consent_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the in-conversation data-access consent flow. AGENT side: requested (the agent asked, so the SERVER posted its consent prompt into the thread), request_already_granted, request_rate_limited (per-thread cap), request_disabled / request_error (the Plain write). CUSTOMER side, on POST /api/support/consent: granted, revoked (withdrawn ahead of expiry), revoke_noop (a withdrawal of a grant that was not live — idempotent for the customer, but not a real withdrawal), invalid / expired (a bad or stale consent link), household_mismatch. Bounded enum — never a per-household / per-thread label. Emitted by SupportResponder. Healthy flow: `requested` followed by `granted`; sustained `requested` with no `granted` means customers are not completing the link (check the SPA /support/consent page and that they are signed in).

panels.title: Consent links redeemed by the WRONG household (24h) — expect 0
panels.description: sum(increase(support_consent_total{env="$env",outcome="household_mismatch"}[24h])) — a consent link minted for household A presented by a household-B session. Nothing is written when this fires (the grant endpoint refuses it), but a NON-ZERO value means links are being shared or replayed across tenants and deserves a look at the threads involved (#2419 security boundary).

panels.title: Cloud-agent dispatch outcomes (#2438)
panels.description: sum by (outcome, transport) (rate(support_dispatch_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the dispatcher-level cloud-trigger outcome, measured at the transport boundary (CloudAgentObservability): dispatched (the Managed Agents session / Claude Code Cloud routine trigger returned 2xx) / error (the trigger returned non-2xx or the call threw — the cloud agent NEVER started) / disabled (the responder is dark, #2265; carries no transport). transport ∈ managed-agents (API-credit billed) | claude-code-cloud (subscription billed). This is the series the #2408 go-live gap needed: the webhook panel's 'dispatched' outcome only means a session was ATTEMPTED — a silent non-2xx trigger failure shows up as 'error' HERE and nowhere else. ALERT on any sustained 'error' rate while the responder is enabled (each is a support reply that never went out). Emitted for BOTH audiences from one shared envelope; the press twin is press_dispatch_total on the Press dashboard. #2416: when outcome=error, the 'Support dispatch failures by reason' panel below splits that bucket into config (a permanent 4xx misconfiguration — a dead responder needing a human fix, alert W6) vs transient (a 5xx/transport blip).

panels.title: Thread-history reads — responder context watch (#2430)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_thread_history_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the per-dispatch Plain thread-timeline read that gives the STATELESS support responder its conversation context (a fresh cloud session fires per inbound message, so without this read the agent answers every follow-up in isolation). PROVISIONING / DRIFT buckets, none of which self-heal — alert on any sustained rate: permission (the Plain machine-user API key lacks thread:read — grant it, docs/ops/plain-setup.md §5.1), schema (Plain rejected the query — a timeline-schema drift), unparsed (Plain returned turn-SHAPED entries — chat/email, not notes or status flips — and NONE parsed into a turn: the actor/entry union shapes drifted). Each of those is also logged at ERROR with the fix inline. NORMAL buckets: ok (the read returned at least one turn — note this measures the READ, not how much CONTEXT the agent got: Plain fires the webhook once the inbound message is already on the timeline, so even a genuine first message normally reads back its own echo, which the API then strips), empty (Plain returned no readable timeline entries at all — rare, NOT the common first-message case), error (a transient miss or timeout — occasional is noise), disabled (the Plain client is unconfigured). The read is FAIL-OPEN — every non-ok outcome degrades to "dispatch with the latest message alone" — so this panel is the only way a permanently context-less responder is visible.

panels.title: Support dispatch failures by reason — dead-responder watch (#2416)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="error"}[5m])) — WHY the support cloud agent could not be dispatched. Complements the #2438 'Cloud-agent dispatch outcomes' panel, which counts dispatch attempts by {outcome,transport}: this one splits the ERROR bucket by cause. config = a non-self-healing 4xx at the Anthropic boundary: a revoked/wrong anthropicApiKey (401), a wrong claudeAgentId / claudeEnvironmentId / claudeCodeRoutineId (404), or a STALE hard-coded anthropic-beta header (400). Those NEVER self-heal — the responder is dead until a human rotates the key, fixes the id, or bumps the header, and the API also logs each at ERROR with the fix named inline. transient = transport / timeout / 5xx, plus the 4xx that ARE load/timing signals (408, 429) — expected noise. ALERT on any sustained 'config' rate (warning rule W6, infra/grafana/alerting-rules-warning.tf); ignore isolated 'transient' blips. Dispatch is fail-open by design, so the webhook keeps returning 200 either way.

title: WifiHaven — Support (Plain)
